stemMarkdown: If 14 men working 9 hours a day complete a job in 7 days, how many days will 9 men working 12 hours a day take to complete the same job? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The job is $14 \times 7 \times 9 = 882$ man-hours. The new team supplies $9 \times 12 = 108$ man-hours per day, so it takes $\dfrac{882}{108} = 8.1667$ days.
altSolutionMarkdown: Chain rule in one line: $\dfrac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \dfrac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$. Everything that supplies effort multiplies on top; the work done divides underneath.
